text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.9% today as oil prices stabilized after several days of volatile geopolitical headlines. Over the past week, the stock has climbed 11.7% alongside a sharp recovery in crude prices—US oil jumped from around $85–90 to $96 per barrel, while global Brent crude sits at $125. Today's move reflects traders digesting conflicting signals: while Trump's reported diesel deal with Russia signals a potential supply boost that could ease prices downward, ongoing tensions in the Middle East (Iranian nuclear fortification, Houthi attacks near Saudi infrastructure) keep upside risk in the market. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher oil prices directly lift both production revenues and asset values, which has driven the week-long rally.

The gap between US oil ($96) and global Brent crude ($125) remains wide, signaling tight supplies outside North America and persistent geopolitical risk premiums—a backdrop that supports crude prices more broadly and benefits integrated oil producers with global operations.
